t.1.185.1: Then, thus addressed, the prince Dhṛṣṭadyumna, foremost of the Somakas, looking greatly delighted, told his father all that had happened and by whom Kṛṣṇā had been carried off.
t.1.185.2: That youth with long, red-tinged eyes, clad in a black antelope skin, whose form is like a god's, who strung the foremost of bows and brought that target down to the ground...
t.1.185.4: And Kṛṣṇā, holding on to his deerskin, followed him joyfully, as a she-elephant follows a bull elephant, while the kings, unable to bear it and enraged, rushed upon him there.
t.1.185.3: And the mighty one went forth unhindered, surrounded by the foremost of the twice-born and honored by them; he strode like the wielder of the thunderbolt among the sons of Diti, attended by all the gods and seers.
t.1.185.5: Then the other, in the midst of the kings of the earth, uprooted a full-grown tree and drove back the throngs of princes, just as enraged Antaka, Death, drives living beings before him.
t.1.185.7: There sat a woman like a flame of fire, their mother, as I surmise, with three foremost men of just such a kind seated close beside her, each like a fire.
t.1.185.6: O lord of men, while the kings looked on, those two foremost of men took Kṛṣṇā and went, shining like the moon and the sun, to the potter's workshop outside the city.
t.1.185.9: Kṛṣṇā took the alms they had gathered, made an offering and gave a share to the brahmins; then, having served that aged woman and those foremost of men, she herself ate as well.
t.1.185.8: Then the two of them saluted her feet and said to Kṛṣṇā, “Salute her,” and having presented Kṛṣṇā they stood right there; then those foremost of men went out to beg for alms.
t.1.185.11: Roaring like dark storm clouds, they told many wondrous tales; those heroes did not tell tales befitting vaiśyas and śūdras, nor such as befit a twice-born.
t.1.185.10: Then they all lay down to sleep, O king, and Kṛṣṇā became the pillow at their feet. Their bed was on the bare ground, furnished with a spread of darbha grass and the finest deerskins.
t.1.185.12: Without doubt, O king, those men are bulls among kṣatriyas, judging by the way they describe the battle. Clearly this hope of ours has been fulfilled, for we hear that the Pārthas were saved from the burning by fire.
t.1.185.13: For from the way the target was struck down and the bow forcibly strung by him, and from the way they speak to one another, surely those are the Pārthas going about in disguise.
t.1.185.15: The king's family priest, having received the king's message, went and spoke words of praise for them; then he, knowing the proper order, delivered to them in due sequence the king's entire message exactly as it was given.
t.1.185.14: Then King Drupada, overjoyed, sent his family priest there, saying, "We wish to know who you are: are you perhaps the sons of the great-souled Pāṇḍu?"
t.1.185.16: The lord of the earth, Drupada, king of the Pāñcālas, wishes to know who you are, O you who are worthy of the best; for, having seen this man who pierced the target, he sees no end to his joy.
t.1.185.17: Therefore declare the line of your kinsmen and your family, and set your foot upon the heads of your enemies; gladden this heart of mine and of the king of the Pāñcālas together with his followers.
t.1.185.19: And this wish has always dwelt in the heart of King Drupada, O you of faultless limbs: that Arjuna, of broad and long arms, might win my daughter in accordance with dharma.
t.1.185.18: For King Pāṇḍu was a dear friend of King Drupada, as close to him as his own self. And this was his desire: if only this daughter of mine might become the daughter-in-law of the Kaurava!
t.1.185.20: But the king, gazing at that purohita who had spoken thus and stood there modestly, gave this command to Bhīma, who was standing nearby: "Let water for the feet and the guest-offering be given to him."
t.1.185.21: "The family priest of King Drupada is worthy of honor; to him a worship surpassing the usual must be offered." Bhīma did just that, O lord of men, and the priest, for his part, accepted that worship.
t.1.185.22: When that brahmin, the family priest, was comfortably seated, Yudhiṣṭhira spoke to him thus: “The daughter was given away by the king of Pāñcāla, who looked to his own dharma, just as he wished.”
t.1.185.23: She, for whom King Drupada had proclaimed the bride-price, was accordingly won by this hero; no account was taken there of social class, nor of livelihood or craft, nor of family, nor of lineage.
t.1.185.25: Things having come to this pass, King Saumaki ought not today to give way to grief and make himself unhappy; and that wish which King Drupada, lord of the earth, has cherished, that too shall be fulfilled.
t.1.185.24: For once the bow had been strung and the target pierced, she was handed over; and so this Kṛṣṇā was won here by this great-souled man in the midst of the assembly of kings.
t.1.185.28: Even as Yudhiṣṭhira was speaking thus, another man, a second one, came there quickly from the presence of the king of the Pāñcālas, to announce that the food here was ready.
t.1.185.26: Indeed, O brahmin, I rightly consider this daughter of the king to be one not easily won; for that bow could not be fitted with its string by a man of feeble strength, nor could the target be brought down by one unskilled in weapons or by one of low birth.
t.1.185.27: Therefore the king of the Pāñcālas ought not to feel anguish today on account of his daughter; nor could that bringing down of the target have been accomplished here in any other way by any man on earth.
